pilot_pr.note: First paint-vm-ascii consumer; established the PaintGlyphRun-per-line pattern and the CliBuilder argv[0] convention gotcha (see lessons.md, 'C#' section).

known_gotchas: CliBuilder.Parser expects argv[0] to be a program name (C/Go convention); language's real args must be prepended with a placeholder, not passed raw.

LoadCow-equivalent file-path building from a user-supplied cowfile flag needs path-traversal / rooted-path-override protection (see cowsay.cs LoadCow for the pattern: GetFileName-only + reject rooted + verify containment).
paint-vm-ascii's glyph_run treats glyph_id as a literal Unicode code point (ASCII-backend-specific relaxation), not a font-internal glyph index -- see spec section 3.1.
Output must be verified byte-identical against an existing port (e.g. Go) for several flag combos, modulo paint-vm-ascii's spec-mandated trailing-blank-line trimming.
Gradle (java/kotlin): must redirect build output away from build/ (collides with BUILD file on case-insensitive filesystems) -- see lessons.md Gradle entries.
Swift on Windows needs the winget toolchain + vcvars setup -- see memory 'Swift on Windows setup'.
Lua rockspecs must pin immutable refs (tag/SHA), not moving branch tips -- see lessons.md Lua section.

build-tool's requiresExplicitPrereqs list (validator.go) is currently {python, typescript, perl} -- haskell is NOT in it, so cabal.project is the source of truth there (must list every transitive local package per lessons.md's Haskell section). For languages that ARE in the list, BUILD must textually reference every transitive local prerequisite's path (e.g. -I../../../packages/<lang>/<dep>/lib) -- use lib/import statements inside source files are invisible to the validator. Verify locally by building code/programs/go/build-tool and running -validate-build-files -detect-languages before pushing any language's cowsay PR; costly to discover only from a CI failure. See lessons.md 'Perl' section for the full writeup.

Swift XCTest: never reference a bare `version` identifier inside an XCTestCase subclass method -- on Darwin (macOS CI runner), XCTestCase itself has a `version` class member that silently shadows a same-named top-level module constant, causing a compile error that only appears on macOS (Linux/Windows swift-corelibs-xctest lacks that member, so it passes locally on Windows/Linux and only fails in CI). Always module-qualify: `MyModule.version`. Found the hard way in swift-cowsay's PaintVmAsciiTests -- caught the local Windows build/test cleanly, only failed on CI's macos-latest job.

backlog.title: Swift cowsay: build paint-vm-ascii backend from scratch, then cowsay
backlog.backend_work: new PaintVmAscii package implementing full P2D02 contract (swift already has PaintInstructions)
backlog.notes: IMPORTANT: unlike Kotlin/Java/Dart, Swift's PaintInstructions was NOT a sealed hierarchy going in -- PaintInstruction was `typealias PaintInstruction = PaintRectInstruction` (rect-only, no PaintPath even). Converted it to a real Swift enum with associated values (.rect/.line/.glyphRun/.group/.clip/.layer), verified source-compatible with every real producer (14 consumer packages build+test clean). Built PaintVmAscii from scratch mirroring Java/Kotlin/Dart, with the Bresenham error term seeded correctly (deltaCol - deltaRow) from the start per issue #12093. Found+fixed two Swift-specific overflow-trap risks not present in any other language (Swift's Int +/-/* traps on overflow instead of wrapping): ceilDiv's scene-size computation and renderRectangle's x+width/y+height extent both moved to Double arithmetic. loadCow's basenameOf deliberately avoids URL(fileURLWithPath:).lastPathComponent (it resolves relative input against CWD, unsafe for a literal '..' input) in favor of manual string splitting. /security-review passed clean on the first round. Verified byte-identical to merged Perl port. Barcode1D's test target fails to LINK in this sandbox (paint_vm_direct2d_c.lib not found) -- pre-existing, unrelated to this change. CI FIX 1 (commit c443453ea5): macOS's build (macos-latest) job failed -- a test referenced the bare `version` identifier inside an XCTestCase subclass; on Darwin, XCTestCase itself has a `version` class member that shadows PaintVmAscii's top-level `version` constant there. Fixed by qualifying as PaintVmAscii.version -- added to known_gotchas. CI FIX 2 (commits 82a9edafcb + 820071814c, two parts of the same root cause): build (windows-latest)'s `-language all` validation failed on 5 PRE-EXISTING swift packages (Barcode1D, PaintVmDirect2DNative, conduit, conduit-hello, IrcServerNative) staging a Rust-built native lib via BUILD_windows shell commands invisible to the Package.swift dependency scanner. Part 1 (82a9edafcb) wired up the previously-inert `# build-tool: deps=...` comment as a validator allowlist -- worked in a plain discovery walk but NOT in actual CI, which uses `-plan-file build-plan.json` (produced once by a Linux detect job, shared across the OS matrix). Part 2 (820071814c), found by downloading and reproducing against the REAL build-plan.json artifact from the failed CI run: main.go's plan-reconstruction loop refreshes BuildCommands per-platform but never populated BuildContent at all (always empty on that path) -- the exact field the part-1 fix reads. Fixed by re-reading the same platform file's raw bytes into BuildContent too. Verified via the downloaded artifact: all 5 swift failures gone, only the 14 pre-existing perl/python failures (issue #12152) remain. STATUS: PR is now BLOCKED PURELY by issue #12152's 14 unrelated perl/python BUILD_windows gaps (confirmed: these fail build(windows-latest) specifically because -language all validation is OS-specific -- BUILD_windows only, which is why build(ubuntu-latest)/build(macos-latest) already passed cleanly for this PR). Deliberately NOT fixing #12152 in this PR (out of scope, different domain, ~14 packages). UPDATE: after several more ticks with zero progress possible (windows-latest stayed red on the exact same 14 pre-existing perl/python failures every single check), promoted fixing #12152 to its own PR as decided in the prior notes. Opened PR #12162 (branch claude/fix-windows-build-validation-12152, off origin/main) fixing: the 14 perl/python BUILD_windows gaps (12 python packages/programs needed `-e ../<pkg>` editable installs synced from their posix BUILD counterparts; python/programs/ircd was also installing the WRONG sibling package on Windows -- irc-net-stdlib instead of irc-net-selectors, a real bug; 2 perl packages had a `REM prereqs: ...` doc line the validator's path scanner picked up as a real reference since only `#`-prefixed lines are stripped as comments, fixed by switching REM to #) AND cherry-picked this PR's own CI FIX 1/2 commits (parseDeclaredBuildDeps + plan-file BuildContent population) since main doesn't have them yet and the perl/python fix alone wasn't sufficient -- validator.go on main lacks the declared-deps mechanism these 3 swift packages need. Also found+fixed a real bug in local verification tooling while working on this: findRepoRoot() in build-tool's main.go only accepted .git as a directory, so running build-tool from inside THIS git worktree (where .git is a file pointing at the main repo's gitdir) walked past the worktree entirely and silently validated/discovered packages in the outer main checkout instead -- meaning every 'verified locally' claim made from inside this worktree all session was unreliable. Fixed to accept .git as file-or-directory, added regression tests (main_test.go). Verified PR #12162 clean via `-dry-run` (real full builds hung indefinitely on rust/irc-net-reactor-adjacent packages during a from-scratch cargo compile in this sandbox -- unrelated to the fix, dry-run is sufficient since it exercises the same validator+diff-detection path CI's blocking check uses). /security-review passed (flagged one false-positive from a copy-paste error in my own review-agent prompt, not the actual file, which is correct). PR #12162 pushed with auto-merge enabled. NEXT: once #12162 merges to main, #12149 needs `git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main` (or just wait for its next CI re-run against updated main, but a rebase is likely needed since #12149 branched before #12162's fixes existed on main) to pick up the fix and get a clean windows-latest run.

discovered_work.title: paint-vm-ascii's diagonal-line Bresenham loop can hang forever for some slopes
discovered_work.severity: high -- infinite loop / hang, not a crash, so it can't even be caught by a try/catch; a DoS if any caller feeds attacker-controlled line coordinates
discovered_work.details: renderLine's Bresenham loop seeds `error = 0` instead of the standard `error = deltaCol - deltaRow`. With error=0, for some (deltaRow, deltaCol) ratios (verified: deltaRow=1, deltaCol=3, e.g. a line from (0,0) to a clip-clamped target (row=1, col=3)) the `row` cursor overshoots `r2` and never returns to it, so the loop's `row == r2 && col == c2` break condition never becomes true again -- infinite loop. Confirmed by direct simulation (not just the Dart translation): the exact same `error = 0` initialization is present verbatim in code/packages/kotlin/paint-vm-ascii/src/main/kotlin/com/codingadventures/paintvmascii/PaintVmAscii.kt's renderLine, and (by inspection, same authorship pattern) very likely code/packages/java/paint-vm-ascii and code/packages/haskell/paint-vm-ascii's line-drawing too -- all three are already merged to main. Fixed in the new Dart port (this PR) by seeding `error = deltaCol - deltaRow` instead; verified against several slopes (steep, shallow, 45-degree, reversed direction) all converge correctly with the fix.
discovered_work.note: None of the merged cowsay ports currently call PaintLine (cowsay only emits PaintGlyphRun, and PaintRect for nothing that reaches this path), so this bug is dormant in production cowsay usage today -- but it's a real hang vector in a shared, already-merged package's public contract (P2D02 paint-vm-ascii) for any other/future consumer.
discovered_work.next_action: issue #12093 tracks the haskell/java/kotlin fix as separate, independent work -- not part of this loop's backlog. For swift-cowsay and lua-cowsay (both building a fresh paint-vm-ascii in this loop), seed the Bresenham error term to `deltaCol - deltaRow` from the start rather than repeating the bug a fourth/fifth time.

discovered_work.title: PR #12162 round 7: 3 more Windows BUILD_windows gaps found by build(windows-latest), after the sql-vm/mini-sqlite #12179 fix pushed
discovered_work.found_during: PR #12162 (issue #12152 fix), round 7 -- monitoring the CI run after pushing the #12179 unixepoch fix
discovered_work.details: build(windows-latest) failed with 6 package failures: python/ir-to-jvm-class-file (issue #12178, deliberately not fixed), rust/embeddable-tcp-server + rust/irc-net-reactor (known pre-existing Windows network-stack limitations, out of scope), and 3 NEW fixable gaps -- python/brainfuck-iir-compiler and python/twig-jit-wasm had no BUILD_windows at all (fell back to running BUILD verbatim under cmd.exe, hitting the forward-slash '.venv/bin/python' misparse), and python/macsyma-runtime's BUILD_windows existed but was stale -- missing 4 deps present in BUILD (cas-mnewton, cas-laplace, cas-fourier, cas-ode), causing pip to try to resolve coding-adventures-cas-fourier from PyPI instead of the local editable path. Fixed all 3: created BUILD_windows for brainfuck-iir-compiler and twig-jit-wasm (translating .venv/bin/python -> .venv\Scripts\python per the known forward-slash gotcha), and synced macsyma-runtime's BUILD_windows dep list to match BUILD. Verified all 3 locally: macsyma-runtime (499 tests, 91.06% coverage), twig-jit-wasm (23 tests, 100% coverage), brainfuck-iir-compiler (74 tests, 96.82% coverage) -- all pass with the fixed BUILD_windows install commands. Confirms the windows-build-affected-set-cascade pattern (see the PR's own commit history/notes) is still producing new-but-mechanical instances of the same 2 known root causes (missing BUILD_windows, stale/out-of-sync deps) even this late in the cascade.
discovered_work.next_action: none -- fixed and pushed as part of PR #12162 round 7. If build(windows-latest) still fails after this push, keep applying the same triage: known issues (#12178, the 2 rust network tests) vs new mechanical BUILD_windows gaps.

discovered_work.severity: medium -- currently just a Windows test failure (build-blocking), but the underlying gap is a real one: this package's symlink-attack hardening simply doesn't exist on Windows at all right now
